title: Feedback sundry brief and feature weave
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Quick synthesizing note from customer calls (Sept-Oct 2025) + CS triage. Intention: capture small-mid sized asks we can probe in 2–6 sprints and a handful of strategic asks needing product/eng scoping.
- Audience: PMs (hosted + dedicated), Eng leads (serving-runtime, optimize), Solutions Eng.

High-level observables (why this matters):
1) Cost surprise is a recurring signal (esp. for customers moving from small PoC to sustained usage). Many ask for clearer, per-route token cost projections and quick remediation levers.
2) Latency variance > SLA windows (spiky tails) shows up for multimodal prompts and longer context lengths. Customers want deterministic knobs (not just “faster” reporting).
3) KV cache visibility: customers appreciate automatic caching but have low visibility into when cache hits/misses occur, eviction root causes, and how to intentionally tune prefix caching.
4) Rollouts & fallback transparency: customers want explicit guarantees and visibility when Redwood routes to a fallback or cheaper model variant. They report surprise about subtle quality regressions during rollouts.

Representative customer quotes (unedited snippets):
- "We love the burst capacity but not the bill — can we see an itemized token-by-route preview before a big job?" — mid-market SaaS analytics
- "Our edge cases blow up latency at 1% traffic. We need some way to simulate tail loads in the console." — fintech platform
- "KV cache is magic but opaque — tell me when my prompt got a cache hit so I can reason about prompt engineering." — health-tech product team

Clustered asks and short translations into product hypotheses (sorted by frequency):
A. Cost transparency and mitigation (high frequency) -> Hypothesis: If we provide a per-route simulated cost preview + immediate mitigations (quantization toggle, cheaper fallback pattern), customers will avoid surprise overages and reduce support tickets by 35%.
  - Concrete asks: token-cost preview for queued/batched jobs, per-request cost breakdown in logs, automatic alerting for spend over threshold.
  - Quick probe: add a cost-preview checkbox to the request UI (hosted) that runs a dry-run tokenization and cost estimate (2-week spike experiment).

B. KV cache telemetry & controls (medium-high frequency) -> Hypothesis: Exposing hit/miss signals and a small UI for pinning cache prefixes will increase cache effectiveness and customer trust.
  - Concrete asks: per-request cache_hit flag in response metadata, eviction logs, TTL tuning in console, and a cache-preview API.
  - Quick probe: include cache_hit in debug mode responses and surface a cache hits graph in per-route dashboard (1 sprint + front-end).

C. Rollout fidelity & predictable fallbacks (medium frequency, high impact) -> Hypothesis: If rollouts show explicit fallback reasons and quality delta notes, engineering teams will accept canary practices more often and reduce rollback frequency.
  - Concrete asks: a human-readable fallback reason string in audit logs, automated A/B quality comparison snapshots, and per-customer pin on fallback preferences.
  - Quick probe: add a \"fallback_reason\" field to recent audit logs and surface a one-click toggle to prefer higher-quality model at cost of latency (2–3 sprints).

D. Latency tail simulation and per-path SLO tooling (lower frequency but high-risk) -> Hypothesis: Allowing teams to simulate long-context and multimodal tails will reduce production incidents and improve confidence in Dedicated/Private sizing.
  - Concrete asks: synthetic tail load runner, better per-route percentile breakdown (p50/p95/p99 by sequence length), and a region-aware latency map.
  - Quick probe: provide a lightweight tail-runner template in Solutions Eng repo plus console button to run it against a selected route (3 sprints).

Feature requests prioritized (RICE-esque quick calc, qualitative):
1) Per-route cost preview (Reach: many PoC->production, Impact: high, Confidence: 60%, Effort: small) -> priority: HIGH.
2) Response metadata: cache_hit + fallback_reason flags (Reach: broad, Impact: medium, Confidence: 70%, Effort: small) -> priority: HIGH.
3) Rollout-quality snapshots (automated evals during canary) (Reach: medium, Impact: high, Confidence: 50%, Effort: medium) -> priority: MEDIUM-HIGH.
4) Tail-simulation runner + percentile-by-length visualization (Reach: targeted, Impact: medium, Confidence: 50%, Effort: medium) -> priority: MEDIUM.
5) Console affordance: one-click cost throttle (temporary throttling to cheapest compatible variant) (Reach: broad, Impact: medium, Confidence: 40%, Effort: medium-high) -> priority: MEDIUM.

Low-friction tactical changes (shipping within 1 sprint):
- Add a \"debug\" query flag that returns cache_hit and an internal token_count_estimate.
- Small console toggle to show last 100 fallback events for a route.
- Add a reusable gist/example to Solutions Eng showing how to measure KV cache effectiveness in customer apps.

Engineering trade-offs & risk notes:
- Exposing cache_hit/fallback_reason has privacy/security considerations for Private deploys; need a permissions gate and SR/Legal sign-off for any data surfaced across org boundaries.
- Cost-preview dry-run needs to mimic same tokenization pipeline as production to be meaningful — syncing tokenizer versions will be required; introduce a version tag in UI.
- Tail-simulation could be costly to run at scale; recommend a throttled / quota'd job that returns sampled metrics rather than full production replay.

Proposed timeline and owners (draft):
- Week 1: Prod-team spike for cost-preview dry-run (owner: Priya Nair, eng: platform-engineering)
- Week 2: Add debug response fields (owner: Omar Ruiz, eng: serving-runtime)
- Week 3–4: Console surfacing for cache hits + fallback log (owner: Benji Wallace, eng: console-and-rollouts)
- Sprint 2: Start rollout-quality snapshot experiment (owner: product-hosted-api)

Open questions / decision points for PM sync:
- Do we prefer to gate cache telemetry behind an org-level flag or make it opt-in per-route?
- What is our policy for surfacing fallback_reason text vs. codes? (text is more actionable but could leak internal routing logic).
- Should cost-preview be available to all hosted customers or limited to those with spend thresholds?

Action items (next 7 days):
- Maya: consolidate calls and add example payloads to JIRA-INV-2345 (done by 2025-10-22).
- Priya: prototype tokenization dry-run and return a sample UI payload (2025-10-24).
- Omar: small serving-runtime PR that toggles cache_hit in debug mode (PR draft by 2025-10-23).
- Benji: mockups for console fallback log UI (feedback from Solutions Eng by 2025-10-27).

Notes to self / raw snippets collected during calls (unpolished):
- "If we could just see a red-line before it charges us, we wouldn't be on support calls." — note: short-term alert template could be useful.
- Few customers asked for a per-embedding unit preview when running bulk indexing jobs — overlaps with Optimize.
- One legal question: customers on Private asked that fallback_reason must be sanitized for on-prem bundles.

Appendix: sample debug response (proposal)
{\n  response_text: "...",\n  tokens: 243,\n  cost_estimate_usd: "0.014",\n  cache_hit: true,        // debug-only\n  fallback_reason: "none" // or "capacity_fallback_to-4bit-quantized"\n}

Summary recommendation (single-sentence):
Ship low-friction telemetry (debug flags + small console surfacing) to reduce surprise + buy time for medium-effort features (rollout snapshots, tail-simulation) which address root causes of latency/cost incidents.

Document history:
- Drafted 2025-10-12 by Maya. Collected customer call notes 2025-09-18 -> 2025-10-10.
- Updated 2025-10-21 after triage with Eng and Solutions Eng.
